Fixed the regression in sqlparse/filters/tokens.py. The TruncateStringFilter.process method had an inverted condition: it was checking `if ttype == T.Literal.String.Single: yield/continue` which meant it skipped truncation for actual single-quoted string literals and instead truncated everything else (including identifiers). Changed it to `if ttype != T.Literal.String.Single: yield/continue` so truncation is correctly applied only to single-quoted string literals, leaving identifiers and other tokens untouched.

Verified manually:
- `sqlparse.format("update foo set bar = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz';", truncate_strings=5)` now correctly produces `update foo set bar = 'abcde[...]';`

The upstream test suite directory wasn't present in this checkout to run directly, but the behavior now matches the expected semantics described in the bug report (truncate strings, but not identifiers).

Fixed the regression in sqlparse/filters/tokens.py. The TruncateStringFilter.process method had an inverted condition: it was checking `if ttype == T.Literal.String.Single: yield/continue` which meant it skipped truncation for actual single-quoted string literals and instead truncated everything else (including identifiers). - `sqlparse.format("update foo set bar = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz';", truncate_strings=5)` now correctly produces `update foo set bar = 'abcde[...]';`
- `sqlparse.format('SELECT thisisaveryverylongidentifiername FROM foo', truncate_strings=5)` now correctly leaves the identifier untouched (no truncation applied to non-string tokens).
